chapter: Four Chocolate Drops, San Diego and Club Royal
title: Musicians in her Club Royal groups
summary: She names guitarist Tiny Mitchell, Herschel Coleman, Norman Bowden, bassist George Mason and guests like Monk McVeal, Lee Young and Dexter Gordon; the job ran to about 1945-46.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So whom did you take in with you?

I took in -- I'm trying to remember who I took in on that job. Well, there's a guy named Tiny, Big Tiny Mitchell, who was a guitar player. A great big guy. My God, he was such a huge man. He was a very fine guitar player. And I think I had another guy named Herschel Coleman, who was -- Herschel? Yes, Herschel Coleman, was a trumpet player, he was a very fine trumpet player. And then at one time I had Shirley -- what is Shirley's name? Well, anyway, a bass player, he was a bass player. Then at one time I had Norman Bowden, who is still around. Norman Bowden is still around town. I would change, you know.

Something would happen, a guy would get sick or something, because I think Herschel Coleman passed while he was on that job. Then Norman Bowden. Then I had another little -- fine little bass player, George Mason, one of the Mason brothers. There are three brothers here, Mason Brothers, and they're all marvelous, excellent bass players, and this guy was the youngest of the brothers. Never studied music, you know.
But he is so talented. He can just hear something and just fall right in, just a natural. He's just a natural.

But anyway, I worked with George and I helped him with his instrument. I didn't have much luck teaching him to read, but I did, you know, teach him chords and everything to play, the right chords and everything, and he was very, very attentive and paid close attention to everything, you know. But at that time he had a family, and I think that was maybe one of the reasons why he just didn't get in to study, you know. Like some people do, they just don't want to sacrifice the time. But he was a natural talent.

But anyway, we did very well on that job, and then at one time Monk MacVeal, Nathaniel MacVeal, worked on that job with me, and Lee, Lee Young worked there. He didn't work too much with me. He worked two or three nights. Dexter Gordon worked on that job once or twice with me. And before I went to work there, Lorenzo Flenoy had worked there, and I think Lorenzo worked there with a little trio or something, and then he got a bigger band and went on to something else, you know. So that's why -- I think that's why the Daniel Brothers got into the scene.
But this was quite a spot. It was quite -- you know. And it was way out on -- around Florence and Broadway, you know. So anyway, I stayed there and --
